account:
Today seems mostly ordinary, but there is considerable talk about the baker and bread. Townsfolk reported the baker carrying wheat at the bakery and a sack of bread at the bridge. I personally saw the baker stock the market stall around eleven and bought two fresh loaves. The baker says eighty fresh loaves are ready for customers and that reliable wheat supplies from the mill would help keep everyone supplied. That suggests active baking and distribution, not necessarily anything unusual. My neighbour checked a rumour about bakery decorations directly with the baker and told me the supposed decorations were only oven glow; I have no independent evidence of decorations or a special event.

Freight approached the baker while I was nearby and asked to discuss a warehouse order privately at the bakery later, asking what time would suit. This is the clearest business I have overheard without knowing its details. It may simply be a commercial order, possibly connected to bread supplies, but I do not know its contents, size, purpose, or whether a meeting was arranged. Privacy alone is no evidence of wrongdoing.

The secretary has been helping confirm my afternoon tea appointment. My neighbour explicitly confirmed three o'clock at the east-bank dockside cottage, road point (16, -60, 105). I should relay that confirmation to the secretary. I have finished my market walk and reached home for noon lunch. Accounts are at one, tea at three, and I return to the office at four-thirty. Tomorrow's ten o'clock mill grain inspection is an appropriate opportunity to ask about the wheat supply the baker mentioned. So far I have no firm evidence of a secret gathering or scheme, only bakery activity, local rumours, and a private warehouse-order discussion.
